I apologize that I didn't explain my Math at the time. I was on mobile!

I used the Rule of 25 and it is an amazing motivation tool. It's the inverse of the 4% safe withdrawal limit rule. It says, take your yearly expenditure, and multiply it by 25 to see what you need in investments to spend that money.

For every $10 in monthly expenses, you need an additional $3,000 in retirement.

$10*12 months = 120 *25 = 3,000. Or 3,000 * .04 = $120/year

I use this all the time:

  • Make coffee at work instead of buying Starbucks every day? $60/mo savings. That's $18,000 less I need in retirement.
  • Cut the cable bill from 150 to 50 (internet only)? that's $30,000 less I need in retirement
  • Reduce my restaurant budget from 600/mo to 180/mo by eating at home more? $126,000 less I need in retirement
  • Sell a car and bicycle/carpool into work (and share a car between the fiance' and I)? $580/mo savings or $174,000 less I need in retirement.

And then you take all that saved money and invest it, meaning it's a huge double whammy - you need less and are saving more. I wish we taught our kids this kind of math. It would help out a lot of people.
